key_boundaries: The theorem concerns a displayed-tree mixture substitution model with uniform root distribution and independent reticulation choices. It is not a theorem about every model of evolutionary history or the network multispecies coalescent.

The failure is pointwise distinguishability. Tree-equivalent theta parameters form a proper lower-dimensional subset, so the paper does not prove generic tree equivalence or generic nonidentifiability of all network topologies.

The theta admits no tree-child rooting. These examples do not contradict results restricted to tree-child or strongly tree-child networks, the retained level-one Kimura results, or the Jukes–Cantor tree–network theorem.

A K3P network parameter with three distinct edge eigenvalues need not produce an observably genuine K3P distribution. The closed-form quartic example has a relabelled K2P output; observable symmetry breaking is supplied by a separate local argument.

Edgewise continuous time allows different generators, rate ratios and durations on different edges. No common generator, molecular clock, global temporal compatibility or standard common-rate-matrix GTR conclusion is established.

The all-leaf theorem gives suitable parameter choices on every binary tree topology and one chosen vertex. It does not cover every preassigned tree distribution, independently composable replacements at several vertices, or genuine four-attachment blobs.

Zariski density excludes additional polynomial equalities only in the effective Fourier spaces. It does not fill the probability simplex, remove positivity inequalities or eliminate tree-model invariants.

Finite exact calculations verify the explicit witnesses and algebraic inputs. Local family and all-leaf conclusions also require the stated analytic and common-kernel proofs; stored verifier reports and AI checks are not formal proof certification or journal peer review.

gap_resolution.location: Published PDF page 12, quartic construction after Theorem 12; comparison factor in equation (17).
gap_resolution.construction_paragraph_source:
The quartic point follows from the positive ansatz
\[
U=(1,b\tau,b,\tau),\ V=(1,b,b\tau,\tau),\ S=(1,\kappa d,d,e),\ T=(1,d,\kappa d,e).
\]
On the slice $\tau=1/3$, the factorization equations force
\[
\kappa=3/\sqrt5,\qquad b^2=1/\sqrt5,\qquad e/d=6/5,
\]
so the positive branch has $b=5^{-1/4}$.
gap_resolution.contextual_restriction: The paragraph derives the preceding quartic point, whose comparison factor B has equal nontrivial coordinates. The necessity statement is read with that same construction context. General positive factorization without this restriction is not claimed.
gap_resolution.restricted_implication: On the stated positive branch M_CC=4*d^2/5 and M_TT=5*e^2/9. Equal nontrivial B coordinates force equality of these diagonals, hence (e/d)^2=36/25 and e/d=6/5.
gap_resolution.broad_reading_boundary: The independently checked e=d example disproves a broader unrestricted ansatz claim, but violates the equal-B specialization and does not refute the selected quartic witness or main local/grafting theorems.
